**Where we are ahead:** the only one of these whose safety is model-checked by a deterministic fault simulator (`netsim`) against all five Figure 3 properties, with positive-control teeth tests, and the model-check drives the SAME `Node` a deployment runs (restart from the persisted state only, Readys batched or not). ## Purpose

Provide a Raft consensus implementation (leader election + log replication) that
is **model-checked in `netsim`** against Raft's five formal safety properties
under fuzzed crash / partition / message-reorder / clock-skew schedules. Modeled
after Ongaro & Ousterhout, *"In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm"*
(extended version) — Figure 2 (state + RPCs), Figure 3 (safety properties),
§5.2–§5.4.

## The five safety properties checked (Figure 3)

| Property | Statement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|
| **Election Safety** | At most one leader per term. | Live: `SafetyChecker.recordLeader` — a second distinct leader for a term trips `error.ElectionSafety`. |
| **Leader Append-Only** | A leader never overwrites or deletes entries in its own log; it only appends. | `appendOnlyHolds(before, after)` over per-leader log snapshots taken each `check`. |
| **Log Matching** | If two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, the logs are identical in all entries up through that index. | `logMatchingViolation(logs)` across all nodes' current logs. |
| **Leader Completeness** | An entry committed in a term is present in the logs of the leaders of all higher terms. | `leaderCompletenessHolds(leader_log, committed)` for every current leader against the committed set. |
| **State Machine Safety** | If a server has applied an entry at an index, no other server ever applies a different entry for that index. | Live: `SafetyChecker.recordApply` / `recordCommitted` — a divergent value at an index trips `error.StateMachineSafety`. |

Each checker has an independent **teeth test** (`checks.zig`) that feeds it a
hand-built violating state and asserts it is caught — so the harness is proven to
have teeth independently of the consensus core.

## The runnable node (`Node`, `node.zig`)

`Node` is one Raft server with no I/O of its own. Inputs: `tick()` (the caller's
clock), `step(Message)` / `stepBytes(from, bytes)` (a peer), `propose(bytes)` (a
client, on the leader). Output: `ready()` returns one `Ready` — hard state,
truncation point and new entries to PERSIST, messages to SEND, committed entries
to APPLY — and `advance()` acknowledges it. The order (persist → send → apply →
advance, persisting `hard_state` before `truncate_after` before `entries`) is
Figure 2's "update stable storage before responding". The node enforces the half
it can see: a leader counts its own log toward a commit majority only up to what
an `advance` confirmed persisted.

Design decisions:

- **Elections are tick-driven.** Every non-leader counts toward its timeout on
  every tick, so a "step-down forgot to re-arm the election timer" liveness bug
  has no place to live (see *Re-arming the timer* below). The timeout is redrawn on every
  reset from `[election_ticks, election_ticks + jitter)`.
- **Terms stop at `types.max_term`.** Decoders refuse anything above it and a
  node there stops campaigning instead of incrementing into an overflow.
- **Senders are the transport's.** `Message` (`message.zig`) carries no
  `candidate_id` / `leader_id`; the sender is what `stepBytes`' `from` says, and
  a sender outside the cluster or equal to the receiver is dropped and counted.
- **Entries carry bytes.** Each log entry's `LogEntry.command` is its
  `fingerprint` (index, term, kind, bytes), so the kernel's log and the
  invariant checkers compare content, not just terms.
- **Rejections carry a hint** (the follower's last index), so a gap costs one
  round trip; also a **conflict-term hint** (§5.3: the term of
  the follower's entry at `prevLogIndex` and the first index of it, or one past
  its end), on the optional 34-byte `append_resp` frame, so a divergent tail
  costs O(terms) round trips — the leader resumes after its own last entry of
  that term, else at the follower's first index of it (`message.AppendResp`;
  the 18-byte frame still decodes, as "no hint"); `nextIndex` never drops below `matchIndex + 1`, and a leader
  retries at once only when a reply moved it (no duplicated streams).
- **Batch decoding is fail-closed for honesty too:** an AppendEntries whose entry
  terms decrease, are 0, exceed the message term or undercut `prev_log_term`, or
  whose index range overflows, is refused (`leaderCommitIndex` assumes
  non-decreasing terms).

**A deposed leader's scheduled broadcast is dropped.** A leader that scheduled a broadcast (`propose`, or a commit advance) and was deposed by a `step` before its next `ready` must not send it: it would go out under the NEW term the node just adopted, as a leader of a term it never won, and a peer could accept it and truncate committed entries (a truncation of its own tail in the same `step` also leaves the stale `nextIndex` past the log). `becomeFollower` clears `bcast_pending` and `ready` checks the role again (`node.zig`): two independent guards; removing either alone is an equivalent mutant, removing both is killed by `node.zig`'s "H1" test. The batched-Ready mode of the model-check (`RaftConfig.drain_every_event = false`) lets several inputs meet before one `ready`, but it does not reach this case; only the unit test does (§ Verification).

## The Fable boundary — irreducible core vs mechanical scaffold

The **Fable-irreducible core** (`safety.zig`, implemented — the Fable pass
landed and `gate.fable_core_implemented` is `true`) is the pure
consensus-safety decision logic. Honest tiering — four genuinely-subtle functions
plus one near-mechanical helper:

- **`logIsAtLeastAsUpToDate`** *(§5.4.1)* — the election restriction. The
  comparison order (term first, then index) is the whole game; getting it wrong
  elects a leader missing committed entries. **Genuinely Fable.**
- **`handleRequestVote`** *(§5.2, §5.4.1)* — grant iff, after term step-up,
  `term ≥ current` AND not-already-voted-this-term AND log up-to-date. Dropping
  any clause breaks Election Safety or Leader Completeness. **Genuinely Fable.**
- **`handleAppendEntries`** *(§5.3)* — the log-consistency check plus the
  **conflict-only truncation** rule (delete an existing entry only when it
  conflicts; skip already-matching entries) plus `min(leaderCommit, lastNew)`
  follower commit. The naive "truncate-after-prev then append" loses committed
  entries on a delayed/duplicate RPC. **Genuinely Fable.**
- **`leaderCommitIndex`** *(§5.4.2 — Figure 8)* — a leader may advance
  `commitIndex` only to an entry on a majority **AND from its current term**;
  older-term entries commit indirectly. This is the marquee subtlety the paper's
  formal proof exists for. **Genuinely Fable.**
- **`observeTerm`** *(§5.1)* — adopt any strictly-higher term and step down. A
  single comparison; **mechanical, implemented in the clear** so the module does
  not inflate its Fable surface. It sits in `safety.zig` for cohesion (it is a
  term/role safety rule), not because it is hard.

**Stepping down must clear `votedFor` AND re-arm the election timer** — two
protocol rules the decision kernel cannot enforce, because both the vote slot's
lifetime and the timer live in the plumbing. Both failures are liveness-only and
produce a node that answers every RPC correctly.

*Clearing the vote* is §5.1's "if `currentTerm` changes, `votedFor` resets" — one
ballot per term. `handleRequestVote` computes its own `effective_vote =
if (term_advanced) no_vote else voted_for`, but that covers **only the message
that itself carries the higher term**: the caller cannot pre-clear the slot,
because it learns of the step-down from the returned decision. A step-down
driven by some *other* message (an AppendEntries or RequestVote **response**)
leaves the next same-term RequestVote with `term_advanced == false`, the
compensation dormant, and a `votedFor` still naming last term's candidate —
so the node refuses a vote it must grant and the cluster burns another term.
The two mechanisms are complementary, not duplicated, and each is pinned by a
test the other does not fail: dropping `effective_vote` trips `safety.zig`'s
"§5.2 … a fresh (higher) term clears an old vote"; dropping `Node.becomeFollower`'s
clear trips `server.zig`'s "a step-down CLEARS votedFor" and nothing else.

*Re-arming the timer.* Every path that sets `role = .follower` goes through `Node.becomeFollower` (`node.zig`), which restarts the election timer (`resetElectionTimer`) and which `Node`'s tick-driven timeout counts from. A step-down that skipped the re-arm would produce a node that is not wedged in any way a crash test can see: it answers every RPC correctly and is simply never electable again, so if the rest of the cluster is gone the cluster is dead with a healthy-looking node in it. That is why the regression test asserts an election actually *starts*; asserting `role == .follower` after the step-down passes either way.

Two additional safety-relevant verdicts live in the core's contract rather than
the plumbing:

- **`AppendOutcome.match_index`** — a success reply advertises the VERIFIED
  region (`prevLogIndex + entries.len`), never the follower's raw last index:
  the log may extend past the verified region with a stale tail an RPC neither
  checked nor truncated, and advertising it would let the leader count
  unverified (possibly divergent) entries toward a commit majority.
- **Vote tallying is a set, not a counter** (`Node.votes`): the
  network duplicates messages, and counting one voter's duplicated grant twice
  manufactures a fake majority — two leaders in one term from a single
  `dup_once` fault.

The **mechanical scaffold** (all real): the RPC/wire codecs and
persistent-state serialization (`types.zig`, `message.zig`), the log container —
append / conflict-truncate primitive / random access / last-index-term summary
(`log.zig`), the server plumbing — elections, heartbeats, vote counting,
`nextIndex`/`matchIndex` bookkeeping, the Ready/advance contract (`node.zig`),
the `netsim` adapter that runs N of those with a disk per server and the cluster
scenario (`server.zig`), and the five invariant checkers (`checks.zig`). The scaffold *executes* the verdicts the
core returns — it never makes a safety decision itself.

**Is there a genuine Fable kernel here? Yes.** Unlike some modules, Raft has a
real irreducible safety core — the four functions above are exactly what the
paper's formal proof (and its reputation for subtlety) is about. The scaffold is
substantial but honestly mechanical.

### Leader Completeness scoping (harness fidelity)

Figure 3 states Leader Completeness for **the leaders of all higher-numbered
terms** than the term an entry was committed in. A deposed leader that still
holds `.leader` inside a minority partition legally misses entries committed in
LATER terms — checking every current leader against the full committed set
flags legal executions (observed live at seed 2 of the sweep). `RaftServer`
therefore tracks each index's **commit term** (the first `recordCommitted` for
an index is always by the committing leader itself: commitIndex advances on the
leader synchronously, before any follower can observe the new leaderCommit) and
scopes the per-leader check to entries with `commit_term <= leader.term`. The
`leaderCompletenessHolds` predicate is unchanged; only its input set is scoped.
A real committed-entry loss is still caught twice over: any future leader
missing the entry trips this check, and an overwritten committed entry trips
`recordCommitted`/`recordApply` (State Machine Safety).

## Durability / persistent-state model

Raft's crash-durability contract (Figure 2): `currentTerm`, `votedFor`, and
`log[]` must survive a crash; `commitIndex`, `lastApplied`, `role`,
`nextIndex[]`, `matchIndex[]` are volatile and rebuilt on restart. For `Node`
that is `HardState` + the persisted entries (`Restore`); everything else starts
over, and the state machine is rebuilt as the commit index comes back (or
skipped up to `Restore.applied` if the caller keeps it durably). `RaftServer`
keeps exactly that per simulated server — its "disk" is what the Readys said to
persist — and a restart builds a fresh `Node` from the disk alone; after every
drain the disk must equal the node's log entry for entry (`error.DiskDiverged`).
`types.PersistentState` remains the byte codec of the durable triple for the
`u64`-command log.

## Malformed messages

Every wire decoder in `types.zig` returns `DecodeError!T` (`Truncated` for a
length problem, `InvalidEncoding` for a well-sized but impossible field) and
validates against the buffer **before** indexing, looping, or allocating. It
rejects

- any payload shorter than the fixed fields;
- an undefined RPC tag byte or `EntryKind` byte (never `@enumFromInt` on raw
  wire bytes). `tagOf` matters most: it runs *before* any decoder, so a
  fail-closed decoder behind a panicking tag read would never be reached;
- an `AppendEntriesReq` entry count above `max_entries_per_msg`, **and** one the
  remaining bytes cannot back — checked before the loop with a real check, not
  a `std.debug.assert` (compiled out when safety is off: a 39-byte message
  declaring 65535 entries would write past the caller's 8-element stack array,
  an out-of-bounds *write* from two attacker-chosen bytes);
- a `PersistentState` log count the image cannot back, **before** `alloc` — the
  same unbounded-count guard as `threshold_ecdsa.PublicKeys.fromBytesAlloc`: a
  16-byte image claiming 1,000,000 entries would otherwise allocate 24 MB and
  read far past the buffer.

**Terms are bounded, and that is all a non-Byzantine protocol can do about
them.** Every decoder refuses a term above `types.max_term`, and `Node.campaign`
refuses to start a term past it, so no peer value can make a term overflow or
wrap. What remains is availability, not safety: one authenticated-but-hostile
peer that sends `term = max_term` makes every node adopt it and then never
campaign again — the cluster halts, safely, with no signal beyond the term
itself. Raft assumes non-Byzantine peers; authenticate the transport. There is
no term-jump bound (*What is deliberately not done*).

**Policy on a malformed message: drop it and count it** (`RaftServer.
malformed_dropped`). Figure 2 defines no negative acknowledgement, so there is
nothing legal to reply, and inventing one would add both a protocol message and
an amplification vector. Dropping is what the network already does to a
corrupted packet, and Raft's liveness argument is built on tolerating loss — a
dropped RequestVote is retried by the next election timeout, a dropped
AppendEntries by the next heartbeat — so a drop costs no more liveness than the
packet loss the protocol already assumes.

The counter is the mechanism that keeps the drop from being *silent*. A peer
emitting only malformed messages is, to this node, indistinguishable from a dead
link; if enough peers do it the cluster loses quorum while every node looks
healthy. **That residual liveness concern is deliberately left to the operator,
not decided here** — the correct response (evict the peer, alarm, stop counting
it toward quorum) is policy above this layer. What this module guarantees is
that the condition is observable. In the harness every byte on the wire comes
from our own `encode`, so `malformed_dropped` must stay 0; the model-check
asserts exactly that across a seed sweep, which is what stops a fail-closed
decoder from quietly hiding a real codec bug.

## Flow control and hostile-peer limits

Three limits were asked for; two are implemented the way etcd/raft does them, the third is not implemented because no reference has it (*What is deliberately not done*).

**Byte cap per AppendEntries — `Config.max_append_bytes`, default 1 MiB.**
The size counted is the frame's entry part: per entry
`Message.entry_header_len + data.len`. *Leader side* — etcd/raft's
`MaxSizePerMsg`, batched by its `limitSize` ("the longest prefix … whose total
byte size does not exceed maxSize … if the size of the first entry exceeds
maxSize, a non-empty slice with just this entry is returned"); `sendAppend`
does exactly that, inside the existing `max_append_entries` cap (hashicorp/raft
has only the count cap, `MaxAppendEntries`, default 64). The default is the
etcd server's (`server/etcdserver/raft.go`: `maxSizePerMsg = 1 * 1024 * 1024`).
*Proposal side* — `propose` refuses an entry larger than
`max_append_bytes - entry_header_len` (`error.EntryTooLarge`): an entry no
AppendEntries can carry would otherwise go alone and be refused by every
follower forever. *Follower side* — neither
reference refuses an oversized AppendEntries in the consensus core (etcd's
`stepFollower`/`handleAppendEntries` and hashicorp's `appendEntries` have no
size check; a limit, if any, is the transport's). `Node` has no transport of its
own, and its decoder already refuses an entry count above the cap, so it
refuses bytes the same way: an AppendEntries whose entries exceed the cap is
dropped and counted in `malformed_dropped` (the module's policy for a message
no honest peer sends, § Malformed messages) in `step`, before anything is
allocated for its entries and before its term is observed. `maxFrameLen()`
gives a transport the largest frame to accept, so it can refuse longer ones
before reading them. A frame above the cap is dropped, so every server must be
given the same `max_append_bytes`, like `max_append_entries`.

**In-flight window per follower — `Config.max_inflight_msgs`, default 512;
`max_inflight_bytes`, default 0 = unbounded.** etcd/raft's `MaxInflightMsgs`
("limits the max number of in-flight append messages during optimistic
replication phase … to avoid overflowing [the transport's] sending buffer",
must be > 0) and `MaxInflightBytes` (0 = no limit; otherwise
`>= MaxSizePerMsg`, the same validation here); the default is the etcd
server's (`maxInflightMsgs = 4096 / 8`, "never overflow the rafthttp buffer").
hashicorp/raft bounds the same thing in its transport
(`DefaultMaxRPCsInFlight = 2` pipelined AppendEntries). The rules follow
etcd's `tracker.Inflights`: an AppendEntries carrying entries takes a slot
(heartbeats — empty ones — do not); a success frees every slot whose last index
it covers (`FreeLE`); a success that covers none while the window is full
frees the oldest (`FreeFirstOne`, which etcd does on a heartbeat response — a
lost message must not wedge the window); a rejection empties the window (etcd's
`BecomeProbe` resets it); a new leader starts every window empty. A follower
with a full window gets heartbeats only (they still carry the commit index and
hold elections off). The window matters here because this leader re-sends from
`nextIndex` on every heartbeat until an ack moves it: before the window a slow
or dead follower would be sent a full batch per heartbeat without bound.

The model-check exercises both limits: `server.zig`'s hostile-peer runs (one
server also sends every peer an over-cap AppendEntries at its own term every 50
time units; a 1 KiB cap and a two-message window) require every hostile frame
to be dropped and counted, the five invariants to hold across a 100-seed fault
sweep, and the cluster to keep committing. The drop counter is what pins the
refusal: with the follower's check removed, the accepted hostile entries were
repaired by the honest leader's walk-back before any invariant saw them.

## PreVote and CheckQuorum

Both follow etcd/raft (`raft.go`: `Config.PreVote`,
`Config.CheckQuorum`, `Step`, `stepLeader`'s `MsgCheckQuorum`, `tickHeartbeat`)
and the Raft thesis (Ongaro 2014, §9.6 PreVote, §4.2.3 disruptive servers);
hashicorp/raft (`raft.go`: `requestPreVote`, `requestVote`, `checkLeaderLease`)
was checked for every rule where the two could differ.

**Defaults: both off** (`Node.Config.pre_vote = false`, `check_quorum = false`).
etcd/raft's `Config` has both as plain `bool`s, i.e. off unless set (the etcd
*server* turns both on; hashicorp/raft has PreVote on unless `PreVoteDisabled`
and its leader lease always on). The module's reference is the etcd/raft
library, and off keeps every existing cluster's behaviour unchanged; README
shows how to switch them on. With both off only the codec (two new tags) and
the `Role` enum changed.

**PreVote (thesis §9.6).** On an election timeout a node with `pre_vote`
becomes `Role.pre_candidate` (etcd's `StatePreCandidate`) and sends
`pre_vote_req` with `term + 1` and its last log entry — WITHOUT changing its
term, vote or hard state (nothing to persist). A majority of grants (itself
included; a set, as for votes) starts the real election (`campaign`); a
refusal carrying a higher term is adopted (etcd: the default branch of
`Step`); a grant for any term other than `term + 1`, or arriving after the
node left `pre_candidate`, is ignored. A node at `max_term` does not
pre-campaign (there is no `term + 1`). The receiver never adopts the term,
never records a vote and does not reset its election timer (etcd: "Only
record real votes"); it grants iff

- it may vote: the request's term is above its own, or equal with its vote
  free and no leader known, or already cast for this sender (etcd's
  `canVote`), AND
- the candidate's log is at least as up to date (§5.4.1, the kernel's
  `logIsAtLeastAsUpToDate`), AND
- it has not heard from a live leader within its own `election_ticks`
  (`leader` known and `election_elapsed < election_ticks`; a leader counts
  itself). This is the thesis's second condition and hashicorp's "rejecting
  pre-vote request since we have a leader". etcd/raft enforces it only
  through CheckQuorum's lease; the module follows the thesis and hashicorp,
  since without it a partitioned node whose log is still up to date (nothing
  committed during the partition) would still depose the leader.

A grant carries the request's term, a refusal the receiver's own (etcd does
the same, so a stale asker catches up). Pre-votes are answered whatever the
receiver's own `pre_vote` setting (etcd does the same).

**CheckQuorum.** A leader with `check_quorum` records, per follower, whether
an AppendEntries response of its term arrived (success or rejection — etcd's
`RecentActive`, set on `MsgAppResp` / `MsgHeartbeatResp`); itself always
counts. Every `election_ticks` ticks (the un-jittered timeout, etcd's
`electionTimeout`) it checks: fewer than a majority active → step down to
follower in the same term with no known leader (etcd: `becomeFollower(r.Term,
None)`); then every follower's flag is cleared. **Lease:** a node with
`check_quorum` that has heard from a leader within `election_ticks` (or is
the leader) ignores a RequestVote or PreVote whose term is above its own —
no term adoption, no reply (etcd's `inLease`). With the default
`check_quorum = false` a RequestVote behaves as before; hashicorp rejects
votes whenever it knows a leader, which would change existing behaviour, so
the module follows etcd here.

**Not taken from etcd:** etcd answers a lower-term AppendEntries with an
`MsgAppResp` only when `checkQuorum || preVote` (so a node that inflated its
term can still get the leader to adopt it); this `Node` already answers every
stale AppendEntries with its term (Figure 2), so nothing was needed.
Leadership transfer (`MsgTimeoutNow`, the `campaignTransfer` exemption from
the lease) followed the same day — § Leadership transfer.

**Wire.** Two new tags, `pre_vote_req = 0x14` and `pre_vote_resp = 0x15`,
the same layouts as `vote_req` / `vote_resp` (the codec versions additions by
tag or by an optional longer frame; it has no version byte). A decoder without
these tags refuses them (undefined tag → dropped and counted), so a
pre-candidate gets no answer from an old server: upgrade every server before
setting `pre_vote`.

## Leadership transfer

Raft thesis (Ongaro 2014) §3.10; every
rule follows etcd/raft (`raft.go`: `stepLeader`'s `MsgTransferLeader`,
`MsgProp` and `MsgAppResp`, `stepFollower` / `stepCandidate`'s
`MsgTimeoutNow`, `hup(campaignTransfer)`, `Step`'s `force` / `inLease`,
`tickHeartbeat`, `reset` → `abortLeaderTransfer`), checked against
hashicorp/raft (`raft.go`: `leadershipTransfer`, `timeoutNow`,
`requestVote`'s `req.LeadershipTransfer`, `ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress`)
for every rule where the two could differ; they agree on all of them.

**API.** `Node.transferLeadership(target)` on the leader (`error.NotLeader`
elsewhere — like `propose`, nothing is forwarded; `error.InvalidTarget` for an
id outside the cluster). `Node.transferee` names the server it is handing over
to (`no_vote` when none).

- **Proposals are refused while it runs:** `propose` returns
  `error.ProposalDropped` (etcd/raft `ErrProposalDropped`, raft-rs the same,
  hashicorp `ErrLeadershipTransferInProgress` — all three refuse). The
  leader's log stops growing, so the target can catch up with it.
- **Catch-up first.** If the target's `matchIndex` already equals the leader's
  last index, `timeout_now` goes at once; otherwise the target is sent an
  AppendEntries, and `timeout_now` follows the acknowledgement that brings its
  `matchIndex` to the last index (etcd: in `MsgAppResp`, only on an ack that
  moved `Match`; a duplicate ack sends nothing). etcd does not re-send a lost
  `timeout_now`; neither does this node — the transfer is then abandoned.
- **The target campaigns at once** on `timeout_now` of its own term (a
  higher term is adopted first): a real election in term + 1, never through
  PreVote even with `pre_vote` set (etcd: "Leadership transfers never use
  pre-vote"). A candidate or pre-candidate ignores it (etcd's
  `stepCandidate`), and so does a stale one.
- **Its RequestVotes carry a transfer flag** (`message.VoteReq.transfer`,
  etcd's `campaignTransfer` context, hashicorp's `LeadershipTransfer`), and a
  receiver honours a flagged RequestVote inside its CheckQuorum lease — the
  old leader included, which then steps down on it. The vote itself is the
  kernel's as always (§5.4.1 included); only the lease is lifted.
- **Abandoned after one election timeout.** The request resets the leader's
  election-timeout period (etcd: `electionElapsed = 0`); if the node is still
  leader when it ends (`election_ticks` ticks — the same period the
  CheckQuorum check uses, which a leader always counts), the transfer is
  dropped and proposals are taken again (etcd's `tickHeartbeat`; hashicorp
  waits `ElectionTimeout` too). Any step-down ends it (etcd's `reset`); a new
  leader starts with none.
- **Repeat calls** (etcd): the same target again is a no-op; another target
  restarts the transfer toward that one; the leader itself cancels a transfer
  under way.

**Wire.** A new tag, `timeout_now = 0x16` (9 bytes: the tag and the leader's
term; term 0 and above `max_term` refused, as on every request). The flag is
an optional 26th byte of `vote_req` (= 1; any other value, or the byte on a
`pre_vote_req`, is refused — one encoding per message), the codec's
optional-longer-frame rule as for `append_resp`'s hint; an unflagged
RequestVote is the 25-byte frame of before. **Upgrade order:** a decoder without
these tags drops both (undefined tag / wrong length, counted in
`malformed_dropped`), so a transfer to — or a vote from — an old server
fails, and the transfer is abandoned after one election timeout. Upgrade
every server before calling `transferLeadership`; nothing else changes on the
wire.

`example-apps/raft-kv` has no transfer command (a client-facing transfer needs a new client op and CLI verb); its `propose` switch handles `error.ProposalDropped`.

## Linearizable reads (`Node.readIndex`)

Raft thesis §6.4; etcd/raft `ReadIndex` with `ReadOnlySafe` (default) and `ReadOnlyLeaseBased` (`Config.read_lease`). A read costs no log entry.

- `readIndex(ctx)` on the leader (`error.NotLeader` elsewhere: like `propose`, the client goes to `Node.leader`; etcd forwards from a follower, this module leaves transport to the caller). `ctx` is the caller's `u64` token. Confirmed reads come back in `Ready.read_states` as `{ctx, index}`; serve the read once `applied` has reached `index`.
- **§8 precondition:** before this term's first entry (the no-op `becomeLeader` appends) has committed, `commit` can lag what an earlier leader committed, so the read waits for it (etcd: `pendingReadIndexMessages`). Then its index is `commit` at that moment.
- **Confirmation:** the leader numbers a probe round (`read_req`, `{term, seq}`, tag 0x17), each peer in the leader's term or lower answers `read_resp` (0x18) echoing `seq` (a peer treats the probe as it treats a heartbeat: the sender becomes its leader and its election timer restarts; an older-term probe is answered with the peer's newer term, so a deposed leader learns). A read is confirmed when a majority, itself included, echoed a number at or above its own: a later probe was sent after every earlier read was asked, so one quorum answer settles every read before it. A reply carrying a number never handed out is dropped and counted (`malformed_dropped`). The probe of a still-waiting read is resent with every heartbeat, so a lost frame costs a heartbeat, not the read. A read the leader never confirms (it was deposed, or no quorum answers) produces no `ReadState`: its reads are dropped at step-down and the caller times out and asks the new leader.
- **Lease (`read_lease`, needs `check_quorum` else `InvalidConfig`):** the read is answered at once from `commit` after the §8 wait, with no probe. Safe only while clocks drift less than `election_ticks` (the lease is CheckQuorum's); off by default as in etcd.
- **Wire:** two new tags (`read_req`, `read_resp`, 17 bytes, `seq` from 1, a request's term nonzero); an older decoder drops them (`malformed_dropped`), so a read against a peer that predates them never reaches a quorum. Upgrade every server before the first `readIndex`.
- **Not done:** follower reads through a forwarded `MsgReadIndex`; the leader's lease is a count of ticks, not a clock reading.

## The positive control

`server.BrokenRaft` reimplements a naive election that declares leadership on its
election timeout **without collecting a majority** and never calls `safety.zig`.
With a fixed (un-spread) timeout every node self-promotes into the **same** term,
so two distinct leaders for one term are recorded — tripping the **Election
Safety** checker (`error.ElectionSafety`) on a clean run with no injected faults.
It reuses the exact `SafetyChecker` the real `RaftServer` is held to, and its
property/shrink/teeth tests (clean-replay, 100-seed sweep, ddmin minimization)
run in the suite. The other four properties are proven to have teeth by the synthetic
predicate tests in `checks.zig`; the real-cluster model-check tests exercise all
five end-to-end. Three more controls, each a deliberately wrong rule the sweep must
catch, belong to the later checks: `RaftConfig.unsafe_send_before_persist` (torn
`Ready`s), `InjectedBug.never_campaign` (bounded liveness) and
`InjectedBug.unconfirmed_reads` (stale reads).

## Membership changes (`Node.proposeConfChange`)

Raft thesis (Ongaro 2014) §4 (§4.1 single-server changes, §4.2.2 removing the leader, §4.3 joint consensus) and the extended paper §6. Every rule follows etcd/raft (`confchange.Changer`, `ConfChangeV2` with `ConfChangeTransitionAuto`, `raft.go`'s `promotable`, `pendingConfIndex`, `AutoLeave`) or hashicorp/raft (`AddVoter`, `AddNonvoter`, `RemoveServer`, `configurations.latest`), and where they differ, which one and why is said.

- **A membership** (`message.Membership`, etcd's `ConfState`) is the voters, the outgoing voters during joint consensus, and the learners (etcd learners, hashicorp nonvoters: replicated to, never voting, never campaigning, never counted in a quorum). It is carried whole as the data of a `config` log entry (hashicorp stores the whole configuration per entry; etcd stores the delta and rebuilds it) and in every snapshot. Wire: three `u32`-counted lists of `u32` ids, each strictly ascending, learners disjoint from both voter lists, at least one voter.
- **Ids.** Servers are `0 .. max(cluster_size, Config.max_servers) - 1` (at most `max_servers_limit` = 1024); `cluster_size` is the bootstrap membership `0 .. cluster_size - 1` until the log or a snapshot holds one. A server added later is started with the same `cluster_size` and learns the real membership from its leader. A config entry or snapshot naming an id past `max_servers` is dropped and counted (`malformed_dropped`), as is a malformed membership.
- **In force once in the log** (thesis §4.1, hashicorp's `latest`): on every server, from the moment the entry is appended — committed or not; a truncation that removes it brings the previous membership back. etcd/raft applies a change when it is applied instead; the thesis rule is what the backlog asked for and what hashicorp does, and the two are equivalent in safety given the one-at-a-time rule below.
- **One at a time** (`error.ConfChangePending`): a change is refused until the previous config entry has committed, the cluster is out of joint consensus, and an entry of this leader's term has committed (etcd: `pendingConfIndex` starts at the leader's last index; this is the fix for the single-server-change bug Ongaro posted to raft-dev in 2015, which a new leader without a committed entry of its term can hit).
- **Single-server or joint** (etcd's automatic transition): the changes are applied together; if at most one voter changes, the result is the new membership (§4.1); if more do, the entry holds C_new as `voters` and C_old as `voters_outgoing`, every election, commit, CheckQuorum and read quorum needs a majority of BOTH (`safety.leaderCommitIndexJoint`, the node's `hasQuorum`), and once that entry commits the leader appends C_new alone by itself (etcd's `AutoLeave`). `InvalidConfChange`: an id outside `max_servers`, no voter left, an empty change list, or a voter demoted to learner inside joint consensus (*What is deliberately not done*). Removing a non-member is a no-op entry (etcd).
- **Who campaigns:** only a voter of the membership in force (etcd's `promotable`); a learner, a removed server, or one not yet added keeps resetting its timer. `timeout_now` to a non-voter is ignored and `transferLeadership` to one is `InvalidTarget` (etcd ignores it).
- **Removing the leader** (§4.2.2; hashicorp steps down after the change commits, etcd steps down when it is applied): the leader keeps leading without counting itself in any majority until the entry commits, then becomes a follower of its term and never campaigns again. Every other path that sets `role = .follower` already goes through `becomeFollower`.
- **Replication** goes to every member (voters, outgoing voters, learners); a peer that joins starts at the leader's last index, active for CheckQuorum (etcd's new `Progress`). Removed servers are no longer replicated to, so one that never received its removal may campaign and disrupt (thesis §4.2.3); PreVote and CheckQuorum are the defence, as in etcd.

## Log compaction (`Node.compact`, InstallSnapshot)

The extended paper §7 (Figure 13) and the thesis §5; etcd/raft (`Storage.CreateSnapshot` / `Compact`, `MsgSnap`, `handleSnapshot`, `restore`, `StateSnapshot`) for every mechanism, hashicorp/raft (`installSnapshot`, `LogCompaction`) where they could differ.

- **`compact(index, data)`** takes the caller's state-machine image after applying every entry up to `index` (copied), keeps the index, its term and the membership in force there, and drops the entries up to it. `index` must be applied (`error.NotApplied`; etcd panics on that) and above the current snapshot (`error.Compacted`, etcd's `ErrSnapOutOfDate`). When to compact is the caller's policy (etcd's server: every `SnapshotCount` entries; hashicorp: `SnapshotThreshold`). Afterwards persist `snapshot()` and delete the stored entries it covers.
- **Restart:** `Restore.snapshot` and the entries after it (dense from `snapshot.index + 1`; anything else is `InvalidRestore`, as is a snapshot newer than the hard state's term or naming an id past `max_servers`). A snapshot counts as applied.
- **InstallSnapshot** (new tag `snapshot` = 0x19: leader term, last index and term, the membership, the image; one message, as etcd's `MsgSnap`): sent when the entry before a follower's `nextIndex` has been compacted. The follower answers with an `append_resp` whose index is VERIFIED, like every success: a snapshot from a lower term is refused with this node's term; one at or below its commit index is acknowledged at the commit index (etcd); one whose last entry its log holds fast-forwards the commit index and keeps the log (Figure 13 step 6, etcd's fast-forward); otherwise the whole log is discarded and the snapshot installed (step 7) and reported in `Ready.snapshot`, to persist in place of every stored entry and to load the state machine from before applying `committed`.
- **While one is in flight** (etcd's `StateSnapshot`): the follower gets keep-alives — an empty AppendEntries at index 0, which matches any log and holds its election timer off — until its acknowledgement reaches the snapshot's index; if none comes within one election timeout, the snapshot is presumed lost and sent again (etcd relies on the transport's `ReportSnapshot` instead; this node has no transport of its own).
- **An AppendEntries starting inside a snapshot** skips the entries the snapshot covers: they are committed here, so they match the leader's log; the rest is checked against the snapshot's last entry (etcd answers such a message with its commit index).
- **Frames:** `maxFrameLen()` bounds every frame but InstallSnapshot, whose size is the snapshot's; a transport that caps frames must allow the largest image it expects.

## Verification

`scripts/modtest raft` (the harness ticks every 10 time units). The module is `heavy` in `build.zig`: the default lane builds it at ReleaseSafe (every safety check armed), because the model-check sweeps took LLVM Debug to 7.4 min; `-Dstrict-debug` forces real Debug. Pure-logic plus model-checking (CONVENTIONS.md §7).

- **Unit tests:** codecs (`types.zig`, `message.zig`), the log container (`log.zig`), the five invariant checkers (`checks.zig`) and the safety kernel (`safety.zig`): one test per documented wrong-but-plausible implementation, including the Figure-8 counterexample and the duplicated-AppendEntries rollback trap. `node.zig` drives an in-memory cluster: election, replication, crash and restart from disk, truncation reaching the disk, hint walk-back, the step-down cases (the stale-broadcast test above), persistence-before-commit, `max_term`.
- **Teeth tests:** each checker has a test that feeds it a hand-built violating state and asserts it is caught (`checks.zig`); `BrokenRaft` must trip Election Safety on a clean run, and the index-only §5.4.1 injection (`srv.bug = .index_only_up_to_date`) must trip Leader Completeness on a directed schedule. The `naive_truncation` injection is not caught by the sweep (an entry's identity is `(creating term, index)`); its teeth are `safety.zig`'s "the trap" test and `node.zig`'s duplicated-AppendEntries test.
- **Model-check** (`server.zig`, real `Node`s inside `netsim`, all five invariants live after every event, `error.DiskDiverged` if a disk differs from its node's log): a 300-seed fuzzed fault sweep; a 150-seed sweep with Readys batched per tick (`drain_every_event = false`); a quiet-network election-liveness run; a directed crash/restart run; the two step-down regressions (a leader demoted by a response or a refused vote stands for election again; a step-down clears `votedFor` so the node can vote in the term it just adopted); `malformed_dropped` must stay 0 in the harness, where every byte comes from our own `encode`.
- **Hostile peer:** one server sends every peer an over-cap AppendEntries at its own term every 50 time units (1 KiB cap, two-message window) in a directed run and a 100-seed fault sweep: every hostile frame must be dropped and counted, the five invariants hold and the cluster keeps committing. The drop counter is what pins the refusal: with the follower's check removed, the accepted hostile entries were repaired by the honest leader's walk-back before any invariant saw them.
- **PreVote and CheckQuorum:** `node.zig` pins a timeout making a pre-candidate that moves no term, vote or hard state; a majority of grants starting the election, stale grants and same-term refusals not; a higher-term refusal adopted; the single-node and `max_term` cases; the receiver granting only an up-to-date log with no live leader and moving nothing; CheckQuorum stepping down at `election_ticks` ticks and not one before, one ack per period keeping the leader, the activity reset each period; the lease ignoring a higher-term RequestVote or PreVote (and without `check_quorum` the vote adopted as usual). `server.zig` (directed): a node cut away for six election timeouts and healed deposes the leader without PreVote, and does not with PreVote (alone, and with CheckQuorum); a leader cut into a minority steps down with CheckQuorum and stays leader without it; plus a 150-seed fault sweep with both on and a quiet liveness run (one leader, at least 30 commits).
- **Leadership transfer:** `node.zig` pins a caught-up target getting `timeout_now` at once and proposals dropped, a repeat call sending nothing, a call for itself cancelling, a follower unable to transfer, an unknown target refused; a lagging target sent its missing entries first and `timeout_now` following exactly the ack that reaches the last index (not a partial one, not another follower's, not a duplicate); abandonment at `election_ticks` after the request and not one tick before; a step-down ending it; `timeout_now` making a follower campaign at once with flagged RequestVotes and no PreVote while a stale one, a candidate and a pre-candidate ignore it; a flagged RequestVote honoured inside the lease by a follower and by the old leader. `message.zig`: the flag and `timeout_now` on the wire and every refusal. `server.zig` (`TransferProbe`): the transfer succeeds (the target leads the very next term and the cluster commits under it) with the defaults and with PreVote + CheckQuorum; a target cut away is caught up first; a transfer to a crashed target is abandoned and the old leader commits again; a 100-seed fault sweep with a transfer every 300 time units keeps all five invariants.
- **Fuzz:** `RAFT_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` runs testkit's deterministic driver over `raft-message`, `raft-tag`, `raft-log-entry`, `raft-request-vote`, `raft-append-entries` and `raft-persistent` (decoders: a value or `Truncated`/`InvalidEncoding`, never a panic); in-suite reach checks run N seeds per harness.
- **Torn Ready** (`RaftConfig.torn_ready_permille`): a netsim `crash_node` is atomic with respect to a `Ready`, so the harness cuts a `Ready` short itself: with the configured chance a server crashes after any prefix of the deployment's steps (hard state, truncation, each entry, each message, the apply loop) and restarts at once from the disk that prefix left, volatile state gone. The 200-seed sweep (both drain modes, 6 % of Readys torn) keeps all five invariants and keeps committing; the control `unsafe_send_before_persist` (messages sent before the Ready is persisted, against the contract) must make the same kind of sweep find a violation, which it does. The order inside `Node`'s `Ready` is thereby checked by the sweep, not only by the unit tests.
- **Bounded liveness** (`RaftServer.checkLiveness`, a post-run analysis; a `checkFn` sees states, and a leader that never arrives is not a bad state): after a fuzzed churn (partitions, link cuts, crashes, no clock jumps) up to time 1500, every partition is healed, every link restored and every server restarted, the run goes on quiet to 2800, and at the end exactly one server must lead, in the highest term any server has, and the highest commit index must have risen since 2200. Holds for 60 seeds with PreVote (alone, with CheckQuorum, and with 4 % torn Readys, where only the progress half is a property: a leader that has just been restarted is a follower until the next election). **Finding:** without PreVote the property FAILS under this harness's deterministic timeouts (seed 6: the server with the shortest timeout, six entries behind, is refused every vote yet re-arms the others' timers before theirs fire, for the whole quiet window); plain Raft recovers from that only through randomized timeouts (`Config.election_jitter_ticks`), which the harness switches off. Pinned as a test (plain Raft livelocks on seed 6, PreVote ends it). `InjectedBug.never_campaign` must fail the analysis.
- **Membership changes:** `node.zig` pins a non-member that never campaigns and is not replicated to; a single-server addition in force on the leader before it commits, after which two of four voters are no longer a majority; `ConfChangePending` for a second change and for a fresh leader before its no-op commits; `InvalidConfChange` for an id past `max_servers`, no voter left, no change; transfer to a non-voter refused; a leader that removes itself leading until the change commits, then never campaigning again while the others elect; joint consensus (C_old {0,1,2} → C_new {0,3,4}) committing only with a majority of both and leaving by itself, with the control `InjectedBug.joint_incoming_only` (C_new alone) committing without C_old; a learner replicating without counting or campaigning, then promoted; a truncated config entry bringing the previous membership back; a config entry with an id past `max_servers` or malformed dropped and counted. `safety.zig`: `leaderCommitIndexJoint` (both majorities, learners never count, Figure 8, an empty set). `message.zig`: `Membership` round trip and every refusal. `server.zig`: a 100-seed fault sweep with a random membership change (single or joint, learners, promotion, demotion, removal of the leader) every 120 time units over 5 servers starting from 3 voters, plain and with PreVote + CheckQuorum: all five invariants hold, at least 100 config entries commit, the cluster keeps committing.
- **Log compaction:** `node.zig` pins `compact`'s two refusals and what remains; a follower behind the leader's snapshot sent it (again after one election timeout when the first was lost), installing it, catching up, and restarting from that disk alone; a server added after compaction joining through a snapshot that carries its membership; the receiver's four cases (stale term, at or below commit, held entry fast-forward, install) and an AppendEntries starting inside the snapshot; keep-alives while one is pending and the resend; `Restore` with a snapshot and every refusal. `log.zig`: the offset log. `message.zig`: the InstallSnapshot frame and every refusal. `server.zig`: the harness compacts every 4 applied entries on every server (the image is a digest of the applied entries, which every server and every installed snapshot must agree on per index — `error.StateMachineSafety`; the checkers see a compacted log as the committed prefix plus what the node holds); a 100-seed fault sweep in three variants (plain; 6 % torn Readys with batched Readys; 4 % torn Readys with membership churn) keeps all five invariants with at least 1000 compactions and 20 installed snapshots per variant.
- **Linearizable reads:** `node.zig` pins a single-node leader answering once its no-op committed (and at the then commit index later), a three-node leader confirming only after the quorum round and appending nothing, a cut-off leader unable to confirm and its probe resent until the link heals, a deposed leader never answering, the §8 wait (no probe before the first commit of the term), probe numbers matched exactly (a stale echo does not settle a later read, a number never handed out is dropped and counted), a follower answering a probe like a heartbeat (leader noted, timer re-armed) and an older-term probe getting the newer term back, a higher term clearing the waiting reads, and `read_lease` (needs `check_quorum`, answers with no probe). `message.zig`: the two tags and every refusal. `server.zig` (`read_period_ticks`): a leader asks every few ticks; in a 200-seed fault sweep (with and without PreVote and CheckQuorum) every confirmed read carries at least the highest commit index any server held when it was asked, and at least 20 come back; `InjectedBug.unconfirmed_reads` (an answer with no quorum round) must trip `error.StaleRead`.
- **Constant time:** n/a: consensus, no secret.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## Performance

Not measured; the card's `**Performance:**` line says so.

## What is deliberately not done

- **A term-jump bound** (refusing or counting a peer's implausibly high term), decided with the references.
  Neither reference bounds a peer's term. etcd/raft's `Step` adopts any higher
  term from an AppendEntries/heartbeat (`becomeFollower(m.Term, m.From)`); the
  only exception is a RequestVote received inside a CheckQuorum lease
  (`inLease := r.checkQuorum && r.lead != None && r.electionElapsed <
  r.electionTimeout` → ignored), and PreVote (thesis §9.6) keeps a *partitioned
  honest* node from inflating its term in the first place. hashicorp/raft's
  `appendEntries` likewise adopts `a.Term` when higher, with no bound. Both
  mechanisms answer the honest-disruption case (a rejoining node deposing a
  healthy leader), which PreVote and CheckQuorum answer here (§ PreVote and CheckQuorum); neither stops a peer that lies about its term, because Raft
  assumes non-Byzantine peers. So no bound was invented: the defence against a
  hostile term stays `types.max_term` (no overflow, no wrap; the cluster halts
  safely, § Malformed messages) plus an authenticated transport.
- **A negative acknowledgement for a malformed message.** Figure 2 defines none, so there is nothing legal to reply, and inventing one would add both a protocol message and an amplification vector; a malformed message is dropped and counted (§ Malformed messages).
- **Chunked snapshot transfer.** A snapshot travels in one InstallSnapshot message, as etcd/raft's `MsgSnap` and raft-rs do (hashicorp/raft streams it, openraft sends chunks); the transport must accept a frame as large as the image.
- **A voter demoted to learner inside joint consensus.** etcd/raft parks such a server in `LearnersNext` until the transition is left; here a demotion is a single-server change of its own (`add_learner` on a voter, alone), and inside a multi-voter change it is `InvalidConfChange`. The same end state takes one more change.
- **A policy for a peer that sends only malformed messages** (evict, alarm, stop counting it toward quorum): that is operator policy above this layer; this module guarantees only that the condition is observable (`malformed_dropped`).

## Backlog / deferred

None open.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class C · oracle n/a

- **Class C** — internal algorithm or data structure — no outside exists, so correctness is defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. Not anchor debt.
- **Oracle n/a** — class C/D carries no anchor debt, so there is no oracle grade to give.

**What the tests actually contain.** netsim model-checking vs Raft safety properties, no wire byte format
